changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md`

- names `renderers/record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

### `.changeset/8400-kanban-name-field-skip-set.md`

- names `record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Deliberately one rung, unlike the same dedupe in `record-details.tsx`, which also carries `deriveTitleField`: that ladder filters a synthesized field list, whereas this one filters an author-declared `cardFields`, where dropping a field the author asked for is a worse failure than a repeated title. A regression test pins both directions, including an object whose declared and derived pointers disagree.

### `.changeset/8649-detail-renderer-undeclared-keys.md`

- names `record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` — the annotation-erasing destructure default is gone from three renderers.** `record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx` and `record-related-list.tsx` each annotated `schema` correctly and then wrote `schema = {} as any`. A destructuring default's type joins the annotated property type at the binding, so `any` erased the annotation for *every* read site in the file — declared keys and undeclared ones alike read `any`. No published surface moves: the exported annotations were always correct.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `0961d5e20` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1374 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1949 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36081195364)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `84039bba8d8a2e2e90530139ace6ff9e1436a0e2`

Rendered by an isolated review subagent spawned by the `domain:ui#4` seat; its served tier was checked against its transcript stamps (71 of 71 model stamps at the review tier). Adopted by this seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) Fidelity to ruling B: kept.** The ruling-B block in `record-details.tsx` ("⭐ THE `titleFormat` RUNG (objectui#8351, maintainer ruling option B)", three outcomes, and "Suppressing on the mere PRESENCE of a `titleFormat` would blind the dedupe") is edited only to say the collapsed value is compared "then against the fields the template rendered". The new second step is `Object.keys(data).find(field ⇒ showsTitle(field) AND formatTitleTemplate(titleFormat, data with that one field set undefined) !== interpolatedTitle)`, where `showsTitle` is whole-string equality of `recordDisplayValueAt(data, field)` with the rendered title. It is reached only through `??` after `titleCandidates.find(showsTitle)` returned undefined, so step 1 is byte-for-byte the old comparison and still wins. A value that merely appears inside a composite fails whole-string equality; a non-placeholder field whose value coincidentally equals the whole composite fails the oracle, because blanking a key the template never reads cannot change the output. `find ?? find` yields one name and one `add`, so this ladder hides at most one row (the Set also carries `hideFields` and live highlight names from above, as before). Empty rendered title, empty record and absent `titleFormat` all make `formatTitleTemplate` return the empty string, so `if (interpolatedTitle)` is false and the unchanged `else` walk runs; `Object.keys(data)` is only reached when the title is non-empty, which the renderer only returns for a non-null record object, and `data` is `ctx.data ?? {}` anyway. One pre-existing asymmetry, deliberately preserved and disclosed ("a candidate match still wins"): step 1 hides a candidate on equality alone with no oracle.
- **(b) The oracle is sound and cheap.** Setting one top-level key to undefined empties every placeholder rooted at it, whether `{field}` or `{field.path}` (the dotted walk breaks on a null step), so the output changes iff that key contributed non-empty text. Edge cases walked: a field used twice (`{a} - {a}`) renders a composite that equals no field, so the oracle is never consulted and nothing is hidden, which is ruling B; `{a}{b}` with `b` blank collapses to `a` and `a` is hidden. A dotted lookup (`{owner.nickname}`) is emptied by blanking `owner`, while `recordDisplayValueAt(data, 'owner')` compares the lookup's display name, which is what its row shows. Whitespace inside braces and double-brace tokens are normalised inside `formatTitleTemplate`, and the oracle calls that same function, so it agrees by construction. A field whose value equals a literal in the template cannot pass the oracle unless a placeholder rooted at it rendered, and when one did, hiding it is correct. Failure direction of the only mismatch I found: the renderer collapses internal whitespace runs while `recordDisplayValueAt` only trims the ends, so a value with an inner double space is never hidden; that predates the PR and applies to step 1 too. Cost: `showsTitle` is the left operand of the `AND`, so the re-render runs only for keys whose display value equals the H1 (normally zero or one), only when step 1 missed, bounded by the record's key count. It is not memoised, but nothing in this ladder is: the file has no `useMemo` call at all (one mention in a comment), and `hideFieldNames`, `titleCandidates` and the first render are all built inline per render, so a memo on this one step alone would be out of place. A placeholder lister exported from core would avoid the re-render but needs a core export outside the claimed surface and a second reading of the token grammar that can drift, which is the dev's A1 argument. Given at most one extra render in practice, I judge the oracle preferable; not demanded either way.
- **(c) The A2 cases are correct and pinned.** SAME VALUE IN BOTH PLACEHOLDERS: `{contract_no} - {name}` with both `HT-2026-003` renders `HT-2026-003 - HT-2026-003` in core and in the header; neither field equals it; the pin asserts the H1 and exactly two body occurrences. TWO FIELDS EQUAL THE H1: `{owner.nickname} - {rep}` with `owner = { name: 'Ann', nickname: '' }`, `rep = 'Ann'`. Core: the empty nickname drops with its separator, title `Ann`. Header: its own `interpolate` returns the empty string for the empty nickname, then `cleanupTitleSeparators` strips the orphan separator, so the H1 assertion `Ann` holds. Step 1 finds no candidate (`name` derives, value `Q3 renewal`). Step 2 walks `id, owner, rep, name, amount`: `owner` displays `Ann` but blanking it leaves the title `Ann`, so it is skipped; `rep` equals and blanking it empties the title, so it is hidden. Pinned by the body not containing `Ann` or `Rep` and still containing `Q3 renewal`. Because `owner` is not in the grid's field list, a first-equal-key rule would hide nothing visible and leave `Ann` printed, which is exactly what the pin catches.
- **(d) The pins are real and can fail.** I re-ran nothing; the counts were checked by case analysis against base `c3025ead2`, whose comparison is candidate-only. THE CARD: `contract_no` is no candidate (the derivation lands on `name`, blank), nothing hidden, `not.toContain('HT-2026-003')` fails. TWO FIELDS EQUAL: `rep` is no candidate, fails. COMPOSITE and SAME VALUE hide nothing on either side, DECLARED POINTER takes the untouched pointer branch; all three pass. 2 failed / 3 passed matches the report and the quoted first message. Ablation 1 (candidate-only restored) is the same 2 red; 3 + 10 (8351 file) + 3 (9436 file) = 16 green. Ablation 2 (oracle dropped, first equal key) turns only TWO FIELDS EQUAL red (`owner` hidden, `rep` printed) with 4 green, since THE CARD's first equal key is `contract_no` and the other three never reach step 2. Both ablations are consistent with the case lists. `record-details.titleFormatNoDedupe-8351.test.tsx` is byte-identical between base and head (`git diff --quiet`); its LIT CONTROL A (template resolves to nothing), B (collapse onto the candidate `name`), C (single-field `{name}`), the composite HALF 1b/2b, the #9436 pointer cases and the no-`titleFormat` CONTROL all sit in step 1 or the `else` walk, which the PR does not change. The new file renders the real `page:header` (registered by importing `@object-ui/components`) beside `RecordDetailsRenderer` under one `RecordContextProvider`, reads the H1 and the body text, pins the desktop viewport, and imports the subject by relative path `../record-details`.
- **(e) Changeset truth.** Every sentence of `.changeset/10360-titleformat-dedupe-rendered-fields.md` is true at head: the header ranks `explicitTitle`, then `declaredTitle`, then the interpolated `titleFormat`, then the unified resolver, so with no pointer the H1 is the rendered template; the blank-`name` collapse renders `HT-2026-003` in core and the header; the base kept the "Contract No" row (red-first); a candidate collapse was already hidden (8351 LIT CONTROL B and C); the comparison is equality never presence; a composite hides no row and two equal placeholders render a composite (both pinned); the candidate scan runs first and wins (`??`); the pointer branch runs first and never consults the template (the `if` on `recordDisplayValueAt(data, declaredTitleField) !== undefined`); the rendered-field step, the blank-and-render oracle, its agreement on the three token shapes, the kept lookup row, and "at most one row" are each true of the code. No line-address citation anywhere in it. One scoping caveat, not a falsity: "blank" in the changeset is what core's renderer treats as empty (null, undefined, the empty string); a whitespace-only placeholder is not blank to core, so the headline does not cover it. The PR body discloses that as a pre-existing finding and the changeset claims nothing about it. The pending `8351-titleformat-hides-no-row` changeset is still true alongside: "answers whether that string is some candidate's value" describes step 1, which is unchanged, and its three outcomes still hold, the collapsed one now for more fields. Both changesets are pending on `origin/main` `0d39dc6e5` and neither is in PR 5400's 400 files, so "in the same release" holds today. The three flagged changesets are unaffected by this diff: `7997-detail-view-related-retired` says `renderers/record-details.tsx` synthesizes a `detail-view` node without `related`, still true (that node is untouched); `8400-kanban-name-field-skip-set` says the `record-details.tsx` dedupe also carries `deriveTitleField`, still true (`titleCandidates` still lists `resolveNameField` and `deriveTitleField`, and step 2 runs after them); `8649-detail-renderer-undeclared-keys` says `record-details.tsx` no longer writes `schema = {} as any`, still true (that default survives only in five renderers 8649 did not claim).
- **(f) Both class-a findings are real, predate the PR, and are not made worse.** (1) `formatTitleTemplate` tests `value === null || value === undefined || value === ''`, so three spaces count as resolved and are emitted; the trailing whitespace collapse and trim leave `HT-2026-003 -`. `recordDisplayValueAt` trims and returns undefined for the same value. `packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts` is not in the diff and is unchanged between base and `origin/main`. With the title `HT-2026-003 -` no field equals it, so both steps hide nothing, exactly as base; the header shows `HT-2026-003` through `cleanupTitleSeparators`, so the duplicate row survives on main and on this branch alike. (2) The header's `interpolate` returns the empty string for an object-valued token (`if (typeof v === 'object') return ''`) and `cleanupTitleSeparators` strips the orphan separator, giving `Q3-042`; core reduces the object through `displayNameOfEmbeddedObject` to `Acme`, giving `Acme - Q3-042`. The header's own comment says it "keeps THIS renderer's interpolation ... rather than core's `formatTitleTemplate`: only its rank moved in objectui#9436". `containers.tsx` is not in the diff and is unchanged since base. The dedupe compares against the composite, nothing equals it, nothing is hidden on base or head. Same class, also pre-existing: the header's token regex accepts neither inner whitespace nor double braces, and for those it falls through to the unified resolver, which is core's rendering.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-detail` is right. objectui AGENTS.md, "版本号策略": "minor/patch **独立演进**——objectstack 没动时不必跟发;objectui 自己的改动照常用 changeset 推进" and "**changeset 里不要声明 `major`** —— fixed 组任一 `major` 都会把全组推上去、脱离 objectstack 的节奏 ... objectui 自身的破坏性变更也标 `minor`(在正文里写清 breaking 语义即可)". Nothing declared, exported or typed moves; the only observable change is that a published renderer hides one more row in a case where it printed a duplicate, a bug fix on a path ADR-0079 deprecates. That is below `minor` (features, breaking changes) and `major` is banned and not used. The changeset frontmatter reads `'@object-ui/plugin-detail': patch`, and `check-changeset-no-major` is among the green checks.
